lines.text: and in the measure of recognition which he attains he feels
that he is strong, whereas in fact he is weak. Whether a man
is really strong and free within is shown by the extent to
which he feels that he is in a position to confess his own
weaknesses and failings. When we are anxiously concerned
to assert our merits, we take trouble to hide our weaknesses
and to gloss over our faults. We easily succumb to bragging
and lying, and especially to a dangerous trick of self-decep-
tion. There are many men who deceive themselves by
refusing to face the fact of their weaknesses and faults, and
flatter themselves by the splendid picture of their personal-
ities which they conjure up. There floats before their minds
an image of what they must be or would like to be, and they
end by fancying that they are so in reality.
The Pharisee too is a man who deceives himself. There are
many various ideals which infatuate the minds of men, for
example the ideal of the quaintly interesting, or the heroic
in various walks of life. The ideal which haunts the mind
of the Pharisee is that of the severely moral and pious man.
He belongs to those who do not shrink from energetic forms
of self-sacrifice, and who do not spare themselves pain and
trouble in order to obey the commandment, what the right
and the good demands. And yet such people deceive them-
selves. All their moral exertion is vain, because they do not
perform what is good from the motive of delight in the good,
of serving others and increasing their happiness, but in order
to be able to praise themselves. It is such men against whose
blindness Jesus struggled; they are the "righteous who need
no physician"-that is, who think that they need no physician
and who rebuked Jesus as a "glutton and drunkard" because
He did not associate Himself with their rigid moralism.
When we have thus pictured to ourselves the type of the
Pharisee, and have allowed to pass before our imagination
the portrait of the man who is greedy for the recognition
of his deserts, the portrait of the man who is self-interested
and loveless, who deceives himself, have we thought and
spoken of others only? of people who are different from our-
